key_insight: Self-supervised pretraining can teach AI models to understand complex neutrino detector signals more effectively, improving performance even when labeled data are scarce. The approach also enables transfer across different heterogeneous detector technologies, moving toward foundation-style models for particle physics.
problem_solved: Neutrino detectors produce highly complex, heterogeneous event data that is expensive and difficult to label. This paper addresses the need for models that can learn useful representations from abundant unlabeled data and generalize across detector types.
method: Pretrain deep learning models with self-supervised objectives on neutrino detector event data.
Fine-tune the pretrained models for downstream tasks such as classification and reconstruction.
Evaluate transferability across different detector technologies and compare data efficiency versus standard supervised training.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that foundation-model ideas can work in scientific instrumentation settings, not just language or vision. It highlights a practical path to better performance with less labeled data and stronger cross-domain transfer in specialized, high-noise environments.

paper_title: Towards foundation-style models for energy-frontier heterogeneous neutrino detectors via self-supervised pretraining
paper_authors: Saúl Alonso-Monsalve, Fabio Cufino, Umut Kose, Anna Mascellani, André Rubbia
